newsitem.title: UK: Lost masterpiece found in former minister's home.
newsitem.headline: Lost masterpiece found in former minister's home.

text.p: A lost painting by Italian Renaissance master Giorgione has been hanging over the mantle in a castle owned by former Conservative minister Alan Clark for decades, a British newspaper said on Saturday.

The Daily Telegraph said the dirt-covered painting "Cupid Disguised as an Angel" is identified in a book published by Giorgone scholar Dr Jaynie Anderson as unequivocally the work of the 16th century Venetian artist.

"According to the condition of the work after it has been cleaned at the Hamilton Kerr Institute in Cambridge, it could be worth between two million-20 million pounds ($3 million-$32 million)," The Telegraph said..
Multi-millionaire Clark, a 66-year-old former defence minister, told the newspaper that the value of the painting was "of no personal interest" to him because it belonged to his family trust.
The rare painting is part of a fresco from the walls of the Fondaco dei Tedeschi in Venice, Italy. Fewer than 20 of Giorgione's works are known to exist.
It was bought by his late father, fine arts expert Kenneth Clark, at auction in 1926. Clark said his father had always known it was by Giorgione but never said anything. REUTER
